meta.purpose: Each case illustrates one differentiation point (D1/D2/D3) or one failure mode (C4 oracle gap)

cases.label: C4 — specificity_loss (DOC code mapping)
cases.summary: Oracle wins because the question needs the literal mapping DOC=52,54 for school district types; joint's evidence contains a ColumnAlias but no value mapping, so the LLM cannot construct the WHERE clause. Illustrates the largest audit category (22/40 cases).

cases.label: C4 — specificity_loss (year column)
cases.summary: Question asks about crimes in 1995; oracle has the exact mapping crimes_1995 → A15; joint retrieves a different ValueMap pointing at A16 (1996), causing a +1-year error in the SQL. The 16pp oracle gap is dominated by such per-question literals.

cases.label: C4 — retrieval_irrelevance (wrong topic)
cases.summary: Question about loan eligibility; joint's top-5 BFS retrieves loan-duration, loan-status, and transaction-type concepts — all loan-related but not the eligibility criterion the question needs. Illustrates the second-largest audit category (17/40 cases).

cases.label: C3 — composition win (atoms-only KB)
cases.summary: Question requires composing 'cards by Aaron Miller' AND 'incredibly rare'. Joint atoms-only KB has both concept atoms; BFS along depends_on co-fetches them. Retrieval can only top-k one — misses the composition. This is one of the cases where stripping composite Formulas does NOT degrade joint performance.

cases.label: C3 — composition win (3-way filter)
cases.summary: Question composes three filters: SLE diagnosis, normal hematocrit, oldest patient. Joint atoms-only retrieves the three ValueMap atoms; retrieval picks the top-5 most-similar bullets and misses one filter. Demonstrates open-world composition under D3.
